Rashi on Gittin 51b:1:1.hebrew: הוא דאמר כר"א בן יעקב - דהיכא דקא תבעי ליה בטענת ברי, לא חשיב ליה משיב אבידה:
Rashi on Gittin 51b:1:1.english: He stated [his opinion] in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov - For where they sue him with a definite claim, he does not consider him a restorer of lost property:

Rashi on Gittin 51b:1:2.hebrew: על טענת עצמו - השתא משמע שאין אדם תובעו, ולקמן מפרש לה בטוענו זה בן המת, דדמיא לדרבי יצחק:
Rashi on Gittin 51b:1:2.english: About his own claim - At first glance, this implies that no one is making a claim against him, but later [the Gemara] explains it as [a case where] this son of the deceased is making a claim against him, so that it is comparable to [the statement] of Rabbi Yitzchak:

Rashi on Gittin 51b:1:3.english: And I fed him a peras - and I returned half of it to him:

Rashi on Gittin 51b:3:1.hebrew: ורבי אליעזר לית ליה כו' - כמו: והוינן בה, ור"א לית ליה חששא דתיקון העולם דמשיב אבידה פטור משבועה, דא"כ שביק לה ואזיל, והאי נמי, כיון דלא תבעו, כמשיב אבידה הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 51b:3:1.english: And does Rabbi Eliezer not hold, etc. - This is like [saying], "And we asked concerning it: Does Rabbi Eliezer not hold the concern for the betterment of the world [tikkun ha'olam], that one who returns a lost item is exempt from an oath, because if so [i.e., if he had to swear], he would leave it and walk away?" And this [borrower] too, since [no one] claimed [it from] him, is like one who returns a lost item:

Rashi on Gittin 51b:6:1.hebrew: אי הכי - דטוענו גדול, טענת עצמו קרי לה? טענת אחרים היא:
Rashi on Gittin 51b:6:1.english: If that is so - that an adult [son] is making the claim against him, does he call it "his own claim"? It is "the claim of others":

Rashi on Gittin 51b:6:2.hebrew: והודאת עצמו - על שהודה לו שאמת כדבריו, ומודה שעדיין חייב לו פרס, הוא נשבע:
Rashi on Gittin 51b:6:2.english: And his own admission - Because he admitted to him that it is as he says, and admits that he still owes him a peras [half a maneh], he takes an oath:

Rashi on Gittin 51b:7:1.hebrew: כולהו טענתא נמי טענת אחרים והודאת עצמו נינהו - ולכך נשבעין עליה, ובכי האי גוונא מי פליגי רבנן עליה? ומי הוה קאמר "פעמים שאדם נשבע"? כל שעתא כי האי גוונא משתבע:
Rashi on Gittin 51b:7:1.english: All claims are also the claim of others and his own admission - And therefore one takes an oath on it; in such a case, would the Rabbis disagree with him? And would he say, "Sometimes a person takes an oath"? Every time [one takes an oath of partial admission], one takes an oath in such a case!

Rashi on Gittin 51b:7:2.hebrew: אלא - לא תימא בטוענו גדול, אלא בטוענו קטן. ודקשיא לך: "אין נשבעין על טענת קטן" — הני מילי בשטוענו "הפקדתי לך", דגבי שבועה כתיב (שמות כ״ב:ו׳): "כי יתן איש", ולא קטן; אבל בא בטענת אביו, נשבעין אפילו לקטן. ולרבנן, אפילו לגדול אין נשבעין, כדתנן בשבועות: "מנה לאבא בידך", "אין לו בידי אלא חמשים דינר" — פטור. ובדרבה פליגי:
Rashi on Gittin 51b:7:2.english: Rather - Do not say [that Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov is speaking] when an adult makes a claim against him, rather when a minor makes a claim against him. And as for your difficulty [that] "one does not take an oath on the claim of a minor" — that applies only when he claims against him, "I deposited [something] with you," for regarding an oath it is written (Exodus 22:6): "When a man gives," and not a minor; however, when he comes with his father's claim, one takes an oath even for a minor. And according to the Rabbis, even for an adult [son] one does not take an oath, as we learned in [tractate] Shevuot: "[You have] a maneh belonging to my father in your possession," [and the defendant replies,] "He has only fifty dinars in my possession" — he is exempt. And they disagree regarding [the reasoning of] Rabba:

Rashi on Gittin 51b:7:3.hebrew: חזקה אין אדם מעיז פניו - לכפור את הכל. הלכך, בשביל הודאת המקצת אינו נאמן על השאר, דהאי בכוליה בעי דלכפריה כו'. וכי תימא: לא נשבעיה אשארא, דמיגו דחשוד אממונא חשוד נמי אשבועתא — אממונא לא חשוד, מדלא כפריה בכוליה; דהאי כי אודי בפלגא, בכוליה נמי בעי דלודי, והאי דלא אודי ליה, לאו דדעתו למיגזליה, אלא אישתמוטי אישתמיט לדחויי השתא:
Rashi on Gittin 51b:7:3.english: There is a presumption that a person is not so brazen - as to deny the entire [claim]. Therefore, because of the partial admission, he is not believed regarding the rest, for he [actually] wanted to deny all of it, etc. And if you say: let us not have him take an oath on the rest, because since he is suspected [of dishonesty] regarding money, he is also suspected regarding an oath — [the answer is that] he is not suspected regarding money, since he did not deny all of it; for when this [defendant] admitted to half, he wanted to admit to all of it as well, and the reason he did not admit to it is not that he intends to rob him, rather he is merely evading [him] to put him off for now:

Tosafot on Gittin 51b:1:1.hebrew: ורבי אליעזר בן יעקב לית ליה משיב אבידה פטור - פירש בקונטרס דמכח מתני' פריך. וקשה, דלא נקט לישנא דלעיל: "ולית ליה המוצא מציאה לא ישבע מפני תיקון העולם"? ועוד, דאין הכי נמי דלית ליה מתני', דהא הכי שני ליה: "הוא דאמר כר' אליעזר בן יעקב", דפליג אמתני'! לכך נראה דפריך: אמאי לא מהימן במיגו דאי בעי שתיק, דמיגו הוי מן התורה:
Tosafot on Gittin 51b:1:1.english: And does Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov not maintain [that] one who returns a lost item is exempt - Rashi explained that [the Gemara] asks from the Mishnah. However, this is difficult, because [the Gemara] did not use the wording [it used] above: "And does he not maintain [that] one who finds a lost item shall not take an oath, for the betterment of the world?" Furthermore, [one could say] that indeed [Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov] does not accept the Mishnah, for [the Gemara] just answered: "He stated [his opinion] in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov," [implying] that he disagrees with the Mishnah! Therefore, it seems [to Tosafot] that [the Gemara] is asking: Why is [the borrower] not believed with a migo [that] if he wanted he could have remained silent, since a migo is [valid] by Torah law:

Tosafot on Gittin 51b:5:1.hebrew: מאי קטן גדול - הא דלא אמר "אלא גדול", משום דבעי לשנויי דלא תקשי לרב "וכי לא ידע מתני'?", ועוד משום מתני' דשבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף לח:), דקתני "אבל נשבעין לקטן":
Tosafot on Gittin 51b:5:1.english: What [does] “minor” [mean]? An adult - The reason [the Gemara] did not say “Rather, an adult” is because it wanted to answer [in a way] so that it would not be difficult against Rav, [namely:] “Did he not know the Mishnah?!” And furthermore, [it did not say that] because of the Mishnah of Shevuat HaDayanin (Shevuot 38b), which teaches: “However, one does take an oath to a minor”:

Tosafot on Gittin 51b:7:1.hebrew: אלא בדרבה קא מיפלגי - פי' בקונטרס: לעולם בטוענו קטן, ודקא קשיא לך דאין נשבעין על טענת חרש שוטה וקטן, היינו כשבא מכח עצמו, דכתיב "כי יתן איש", ואין נתינת קטן כלום; אבל בא בטענת אביו, טענה חשובה היא, וטעמא דרבנן כדרבה, משום דבבנו מעיז. וקשה, דעיקר התירוץ חסר מן הספר! ועוד, דבהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף קו:) ממעט נתנו כשהוא קטן וטענו כשהוא גדול, משום דבעינן תביעה ונתינה כאחת שוין; וא"כ מהאי טעמא נמי נמעט נתנו כשהוא גדול ותבעו כשהוא קטן, דהיינו בבא בטענת אביו! לכך נראה לפרש דקאי אמאי דקאמר "טענת עצמו? טענת אחרים הוא" — הא דקרי לה טענת עצמו, משום דבבנו מעיז ומעיז וכדרבנן; אע"ג דראב"י סבר דבבנו נמי אינו מעיז, הכי קאמר להו לרבנן: פעמים שאדם נשבע על מה שאתם מחשיבין טענת עצמו:
Tosafot on Gittin 51b:7:1.english: Rather, they disagree with regard to Rabba’s [explanation] - Rashi explained: Actually, [the Mishnah is dealing with a case] where a [real] minor makes the claim against him; and as for what was difficult to you — that one does not take an oath based on the claim of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor — that applies [only] when he comes on his own behalf, as it is written, "If a man delivers," and a minor’s delivery is nothing; however, when he comes with his father’s claim, it is a significant claim, and the Rabbis’ reason is in accordance with Rabba’s [principle], because toward [the creditor’s] son [the debtor] is brazen. But this is difficult, for the main part of the answer is missing from the text! Furthermore, in [the chapter] Hagozel Kama (Bava Kamma 106b), [the Gemara] excludes [a case where] he gave it when he was a minor and claimed it when he was an adult, because we require the claim and the delivery to be alike as one; and if so, for that same reason we should also exclude [a case where] he gave it when he was an adult and he claimed it when he was a minor — which is [the case of] one who comes with his father’s claim! Therefore, it seems [best] to explain that [this statement] refers back to what [the Gemara] said: "[Is it] his own claim? It is the claim of others!" — the reason [Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov] calls it "his own claim" is because toward his son he is completely brazen, in accordance with the Rabbis’ [view]; even though Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov holds that toward his son as well he is not brazen, this is what he is saying to the Rabbis: Sometimes a person takes an oath over what you consider "his own claim":

Tosafot on Gittin 51b:7:2.hebrew: מפני מה אמרה תורה מודה מקצת הטענה ישבע - פי': למה לא יהא נאמן במיגו דאי בעי כופר הכל, או נילף מהכא דלא אמרינן מיגו? ומשני, דאין אדם מעיז פניו בפני בעל חובו, וליכא מיגו, דאין לו פנים לכפור הכל. אע"ג דבכופר הכל אמרינן נמי בפ' הדיינין (שבועות דף מ:) דאשתמוטי קא משתמיט, דלכך נתקנה שבועת היסת בכופר הכל, מ"מ יותר יש לו פנים לכפור מקצת מלכפור הכל, וליכא מיגו. אבל אין לפרש שבא ליתן טעם אמאי כופר הכל פטור, וקאמר לפי שאין אדם מעיז; דהא כופר הכל פטור אפילו במקום שיכול להעיז, דהרי בבנו דמעיז פטרוהו רבנן אפילו מודה מקצת במיגו דאי בעי כופר הכל. וכן בפ"ק דב"מ (דף ד:) גבי סילעין דינרין, פטר [ר"ע] בלוה אומר ג', משום דמשיב אבידה, דאי בעי אמר ב' והוי כופר הכל, דהא דכתיב בשטר כהילך דמי. ופריך נמי מינה התם למאן דאמר הילך חייב — אלמא כופר הכל פטור, ואע"ג דיכול להעיז משום דמסייע ליה שטרא, דהא פטור במודה במקצת במיגו דאי בעי כפר הכל. וכופר הכל דפטור, גזירת הכתוב, דכתיב "כי הוא זה" — משמע דוקא במודה במקצת ולא כופר הכל, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דב"מ (דף ה.), דתרי קראי כתיבי: כתיב "הוא" וכתיב "זה". אבל מדחייביה רחמנא שבועה בעד אחד אין להוכיח דכופר הכל פטור, דאי חייב מאי נפקא מינה מעד אחד כיון דבלאו הכי חייב שבועה? דאיצטריך להיכא שאין הבעלים יודעין, והעד מעיד שגנב לו או שהיה חייב לאביו:
Tosafot on Gittin 51b:7:2.english: For what reason did the Torah say that one who admits to part of the claim takes an oath - Meaning: Why should he not be believed with a migo [argument], that if he wanted he could deny everything, or [why should we not] learn from here that we do not apply migo? And [the Gemara] answers that a person would not be so brazen as to stand before his creditor, and [thus] there is no migo, because he does not have the nerve to deny everything. Even though regarding one who denies everything we also say in the chapter [entitled] HaDayanin (Shevuot 40b) that he is [merely] trying to evade [payment] — for which reason the hesset oath was instituted for one who denies everything — nevertheless, he has more nerve to deny part than to deny everything, and [therefore] there is no migo. However, one should not explain that [Rabba] comes to give a reason why one who denies everything is exempt, saying [that it is] because a person is not brazen; for one who denies everything is exempt even in a case where he is able to be brazen, for behold, regarding [a claim against] his [creditor's] son, where he is brazen, the Rabbis exempted him even when he admits to part, with a migo that if he wanted he could deny everything. And similarly, in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (4b), regarding [the case of] selaim [and] dinars, [Rabbi Akiva] exempted [the borrower] where the borrower says three [selaim], because he is [like] one who returns a lost object; for if he wanted he could have said two, and he would be [considered] one who denies everything, since what is written in the document is like "here it is" (heilakh). And [the Gemara] also raises an objection from it there against the one who says [that] "here it is" is liable — thus [we see that] one who denies everything is exempt, even though he is able to be brazen because the document supports him, for he is exempt when admitting to part with a migo that if he wanted he could deny everything. And [the rule] that one who denies everything is exempt is a scriptural decree, for it is written, "that this is it" (ki hu zeh) — implying specifically one who admits to part and not one who denies everything, as we say in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (5a), that two [expressions] are written in the verse: "it" (hu) is written and "this" (zeh) is written. However, from [the fact] that the Merciful One obligated him [to take] an oath through a single witness, one cannot prove that one who denies everything is exempt — [arguing] that if he were liable, what practical difference would there be from a single witness, since even without that he would be obligated [to take] an oath? — because it is needed for a case where the owner does not know [of the claim], and the witness testifies that [the defendant] stole from him or that he owed his father:

Tosafot on Gittin 51b:7:3.hebrew: אין אדם מעיז - אין לפרש לפי שעשה לו טובה כדפי' בקונטרס בהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף קז.), דאם כן, בפקדון שלא עשה לו טובה, יפטר במודה במקצת במיגו דאי בעי כפר הכל; ובכמה דוכתי מחייבינן מודה במקצת בפקדון! אלא אין אדם מעיז כל מקום שאותו שכנגדו יודע שהוא משקר, כדפי' ריב"א, ואין להאריך כאן:
Tosafot on Gittin 51b:7:3.english: A person is not brazen - One should not explain [that this is] because he did him a favor, as Rashi explained in [the chapter] HaGozel Kamma (Bava Kamma 107a) — for if so, in [the case of] a deposit, where he did not do him a favor, he would be exempt in [a case of] partial admission by [virtue of] a migo, since if he wanted he could have denied everything; yet in several places we obligate one who makes a partial admission regarding a deposit! Rather, a person is not brazen in any situation where the one opposite him knows that he is lying, as Riva explained, and there is no [need] to elaborate here:

Tosafot on Gittin 51b:8:1.hebrew: ובכולי בעי דלודי ליה - פי' בקונטרס: וכי תימא דלא נשבעיניה אשארא, דמיגו דחשיד אממונא חשיד אשבועתא — אממונא לא חשיד, מדלא כפריה כוליה, וכי היכי דמודה בפלגא, בכוליה נמי בעי דלודי ליה. וקשה, דבפ"ק דב"מ (דף ו.) מסקינן דלא אמרינן מיגו דחשיד אממונא חשיד אשבועתא. וליכא למימר דהתם מדרבנן הוא דלא חשיד, לפי שראו דפריש משבועתא טפי מממונא, דהא משמע בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף לג:) גבי נסכא דרבי אבא, דאי הוה אמר "לא חטפי", הוה נשבע להכחיש את העד; אלמא לא אמרינן מיגו דחשוד אממונא חשוד נמי אשבועתא. וההיא שבועה דאורייתא, דשבועה דרבנן לא אמרינן מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם, דתקנתא לתקנתא לא עבדינן, כדאמרינן גבי ההוא רעיא בבבא מציעא בפ"ק (דף ה.). לכן נראה דאתא לפרש, דלא תימא: כיון דאין אדם מעיז פניו, אם כן קושטא קאמר, ויפטר משבועה מאותו מקצת שכופר מטעם חזקה דאין אדם מעיז; ולהכי קאמר "ובכולי הוא דבעי דלודי ליה", דאינו ברצון מעיז, אלא אישתמוטי קא מישתמיט. ואם תאמר: גזלן אמאי פסול לשבועה, כיון דלא אמרינן מיגו דחשיד אממונא חשיד נמי אשבועתא? וי"ל דמדרבנן פסול, משום דפסלתו תורה לעדות, דכתיב "להיות עד חמס"; ולא גזרו רבנן אלא היכא דנודע פסולו, דגנאי הוא להשביעו. ואם תאמר: מדאורייתא, מאי שנא לאו דעדות מלאו דשבועה? וי"ל דחמירא ליה שבועה, לפי שכל העולם נזדעזע בשעה שאמר הקדוש ברוך הוא "לא תשא", כדאמרינן בריש פרק הדיינין (שבועות דף לט.). ועוד יש לחלק, דעל אותו ממון דחשדינן ליה לא חשיד אשבועתא, דעל ידי שבועה יפרוש; אבל גזלן אממון אחר חשוד, כמו שמממון אחר לא פירש, כמו כן לא יפרוש משבועה. ולא קשה מההוא רעיא דאסהידו ביה דאכל תרי מנייהו, אמאי פסול, דהנך תרי צריך לשלם ומן השאר יפרוש על ידי שבועה? דהא מה שמשלם ע"י עדים, אין זה השבה מעליא, דעל כורחו הוא משלם:
Tosafot on Gittin 51b:8:1.english: And he wants to admit to all of it to him - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: And if you say that we should not administer an oath to him regarding the rest, because since he is suspect regarding money, he is suspect regarding an oath — he is not suspect regarding money, since he did not deny all of it; and just as he admits to half, he also wants to admit to all of it to him. And this is difficult, for in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (6a) we conclude that we do not say [that] since he is suspect regarding money, he is suspect regarding an oath. And one cannot say that there it is [only] by rabbinic law that he is not suspect, because [the Sages] saw that he refrains from [a false] oath more than from [stealing] money; for it is implied in [the chapter entitled] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 33b), regarding the silver ingot of Rabbi Abba, that if [the defendant] had said, "I did not snatch [it]," he would have sworn to contradict the witness — thus, we do not say [that] since he is suspect regarding money, he is also suspect regarding an oath! And that oath [there in Bava Batra] is biblical, for [regarding] a rabbinic oath we do not say "since he cannot swear, he pays," because we do not make an enactment upon an enactment, as we say regarding that shepherd in Bava Metzia in the first chapter (5a). Therefore, it seems that [the Gemara] comes to explain [this] so that you should not say: since a person is not brazen, if so, he is speaking the truth, and he should be exempt from an oath regarding that portion that he denies, on the basis of the presumption that a person is not brazen. Therefore [the Gemara] says, "And he wants to admit to all of it to him" — that he is not brazenly denying [the debt] willingly, rather he is [merely] evading [him temporarily]. And if you say: Why is a robber disqualified from [taking] an oath, since we do not say [that] since he is suspect regarding money, he is also suspect regarding an oath? One can say that he is disqualified by rabbinic law, because the Torah disqualified him from testimony, as it is written, "to be a malicious witness"; and the Rabbis only decreed [this] where his disqualification is known, for it is disgraceful to administer an oath to him. And if you say: Under biblical law, what is the difference between the prohibition of [false] testimony and the prohibition of [a false] oath? One can say that an oath is more severe to him, because the entire world trembled at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, said, "You shall not take [the name of the Lord in vain]," as we say at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] HaDayanim (Shevuot 39a). And furthermore, one can distinguish [as follows]: regarding that [same] money of which we suspect him, he is not suspect regarding an oath, for through an oath he will refrain [from taking it]; however, a robber is suspect regarding other money — just as he did not refrain from [taking] other money, so too he will not refrain from [a false] oath. And there is no difficulty from that shepherd against whom [witnesses] testified that he ate two of them, [asking] why he is disqualified [from taking an oath], since he must pay for those two and from the rest he would refrain [from taking] on account of an oath — for that which he pays through witnesses is not a proper restitution, since he pays against his will:
